messages:
emma.support: Customer (Acme Ads) opened a support ticket: p99 latency for /v1/generate jumped ~2.1x after maintenance window (weekend CUDA stack update). No increase in errors, just tail latency. They see spikes only on dedicated-usw2 pool.

maria-cs: forwarding notes from customer: they reported RTTs moving from ~140ms p99 to ~330ms. Happens across multiple instances, not all traffic. No request size change.

ajay.eng-runtime: thanks. any kernel or driver rollouts scheduled for that window?

julia.eng-infra: we did a CUDA 12.2.5 -> 13.0.1 driver+libcudnn push to dedicated-usw2 madrugada Saturday 03:10 UTC. Small firmware bump on some nodes too.

kai.eng-sre: hooking in. Can we repro on a canary node? also need NVMe qdepth + host kernel preempt stats.

emma.support: customer provided traces and a short repro script (they called our SDK at 10 qps, batch_size=1). I pasted logs below.

emma.support: ```
REQUEST_IDS: [r-01e2, r-01e3, r-01e4]
p95: 110ms before, p95 now: 240ms
p99: 140ms before, p99 now: 330ms
no 5xxs, no auth errors
```

ajay.eng-runtime: can you run this quick check on a suspected host: `nvidia-smi topo -m && dmesg | tail -n50` and also collect `iostat -x 1 5` during repro? Kernel preemptible workload might be causing tail spikes for tiny batches.

julia.eng-infra: ran quick probe on 3 repro nodes: NVMe iowait shows bursty stalls at times of spike, queue_depth occasionally hits 128, host kernel reports blk_mq dispatch delays. Also see a handful of WARNs from the new GPU firmware: `GPU NVLINK timeout` (intermittent).

kai.eng-sre: that matches p99 noise from storage interference + firmware interactions. Two mitigation paths: 1) rollback CUDA+firmware on a small canary and compare, 2) apply cgroup io.weight limits / reduce qdepth for the inference container class.

ajay.eng-runtime: we should also pin model runtime to keep smaller sequence handling on fast path. Suggest forcing batch aggregation window to 10ms for dedicated-usw2 to reduce small-batch overhead while we triage.

emma.support: customer asked for a quick rollback if we confirm. Are we confident this is infra-level and not model change?

ajay.eng-runtime: no model changes deployed there. I think infra. Steps to repro/triage for SRE + Infra: 
1) Reproduce with customer script against a canary host annotated with old vs new drivers.
2) Collect `perf record` short trace during spike and compare syscalls latency.
3) Run `iostat -x 1 10` + `nvidia-smi pmon -s u` during run.
4) If NVMe qdepth hits high, apply tentative cgroup throttling: `echo "300" > /sys/fs/cgroup/io/inference.slice/io.max` (dry-run).

julia.eng-infra: will start a canary rollback tonight (UTC) on 2 nodes and run customer's script. ETA 4h. If rollback improves p99 by >30% we will widen. Also will attempt firmware reflash for 1 node.

kai.eng-sre: I will prepare an emergency routing policy to divert traffic off affected nodes if p99 > 250ms for > 5m. Add an automated fallback to older model variant too.

emma.support: tagged customer: we'll update in ~6h with findings. thanks all. :pray:

deploy-bot: Rolling back driver on node gw-usw2-23 (canary) -> scheduling maintenance window 03:15 UTC.

julia.eng-infra: quick note from canary run: after rolling back to CUDA 12.2.5 driver + previous firmware, we reran the customer's script. p99 dropped from ~335ms to ~155ms on the canary. NVMe qdepth never exceeded 32.

ajay.eng-runtime: good signal. looks like the new stack exposed host-kernel scheduling/blk_mq corner-case under our tiny-batch workload. Planning a targeted mitigation: 1) rollback cluster-wide for Dedicated-usw2 (after approvals), 2) add qdepth guardrails and batch-window tweak to reduce sensitivity.

maria-cs: customer is relieved, asked for timeline to full rollback and whether their traffic will be affected during the rollback.

kai.eng-sre: drafting rollback plan and blackout window. recommend rolling nodes out in 5% increments with health checks: synthetic p99 < 180ms for 10m.

emma.support: action items summarized: 
- julia: finalize rollback plan + firmware flash schedule (in 2h)
- kai: prepare routing fallback policy & health checks
- ajay: ship temporary batch-window change and qdepth guard in config for dedicated-usw2
- maria: keep customer updated, share repro checklist and outcome

ajay.eng-runtime: putting a hotfix change to config now: set aggregation_ms=10 for dedicated-usw2, and limit per-container qdepth via runtime cgroup helper. Will notify when live.

julia.eng-infra: rollback queued, starting 5% node group now. monitoring dashboard link: https://console/redwood-dashboards/d/infra/driver-rollback-usw2

emma.support: thanks everyone. will close the loop once rollback completes and customer confirms.

maria-cs: customer posted: "thanks — tail latencies look back to normal on our side during testing" :tada:

kai.eng-sre: leaving note for postmortem: root cause = interaction between CUDA 13 driver+gpu firmware and host blk_mq under tiny-batch inference patterns -> led to NVMe dispatch stalls and p99 spikes. Mitigations: rollback, qdepth/cgroup guardrails, batch aggregation SLO.

emma.support: assigning follow-up PM/POSTMORTEM -> eng-infra + eng-runtime + eng-sre.
